comments.author: @Bluejay1122
comments.text:
It is illegal for companies to raise prices to post a lower price and call it a sale or clearance.
Information/
The practice tricks consumers into believing they are getting an extraordinary bargain. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) regulates this under its Guides Against Deceptive Pricing. According to the FTC, a former reference price must be a legitimate price at which the product was actively sold for a reasonably substantial period of time.

Raising a price purely to support a fake "marked down" claim violates federal trade laws and can also subject retailers to class-action lawsuits and state-level consumer protection enforcement.
